name: East India Company
description: English joint-stock company that became a territorial power in India.

name: Robert Clive
description: Company officer and victor at Plassey; later Governor of Bengal.

name: Warren Hastings
description: First Governor-General of Bengal; impeached 1787 and acquitted 1795.

name: Mir Jafar
description: Commander who aided the Company at Plassey and became Nawab of Bengal.

name: British Parliament
description: Legislature that regulated and eventually absorbed the Company.

name: British Crown
description: Assumed direct rule of India in 1858.

name: Anglo-Iranian Oil Company (later BP)
description: British oil company whose Iranian concession was nationalized in 1951.

name: Mohammad Mossadegh
description: Prime Minister of Iran 1951-1953.

name: Mohammad Reza Pahlavi
description: Shah of Iran, restored to full power after the 1953 coup.

name: Central Intelligence Agency
description: US agency that planned and directed Operation Ajax.

name: MI6 (Secret Intelligence Service)
description: British agency that co-planned the coup (Operation Boot).

name: Kermit Roosevelt Jr.
description: CIA officer who led the field operation in Tehran.

name: Fazlollah Zahedi
description: General installed as prime minister after the coup.

name: Government of Iran
description: Nationalized the oil industry in 1951.

name: Allen W. Dulles
description: Director of Central Intelligence from 1953 to 1961; brother of John Foster Dulles.

name: John Foster Dulles
description: US Secretary of State, 1953–1959; brother of Allen W. Dulles.

name: US Department of State
description: US foreign-policy department led by John Foster Dulles during the 1953 Iran crisis.

name: George Grenville
description: British prime minister whose ministry pursued postwar colonial revenue and the 1765 Stamp Act.

name: Thomas Hutchinson
description: Royal governor of Massachusetts who refused to allow East India Company tea ships to depart Boston in 1773 without meeting customs requirements.

name: First Continental Congress
description: Assembly of representatives from British mainland North American colonies convened in Philadelphia in September 1774 to coordinate grievances and responses to British policy.

name: Boston tea protest movement
description: Colonial organizers and participants opposing tea policy in Boston; not a single uniform organization or ideology.

name: Pontiac
description: Ottawa leader associated with a coordinated Indigenous resistance movement against British military posts and settler expansion after the Seven Years' War.

name: Virginia colonial land investors
description: A category of land speculators and companies seeking western territorial claims, rather than a single coordinated body.

name: Massachusetts colonial militias
description: Locally organized militia companies that opposed British regular troops at Lexington and Concord in April 1775.
